title: Boreen Point and Lake Cootharaba

bikeon.heading: Boreen Point and Lake Cootharaba
paras: Lake Cootharaba is the biggest lake on the Noosa River, roughly 10 kilometres long, about 25 kilometres around and on average only about a metre and a half deep. The river enters from the north through the Noosa Everglades system, often described as one of only two everglades in the world, and leaves to the south towards Noosa Heads. Kin Kin Creek feeds the top of the lake. The Queensland Government records several possible meanings for Cootharaba, including the Indigenous name for the lake, a place where wood for notched or studded clubs could be found. In 1870 a timber company, McGhie, Luya and Co, took up land at Mill Point, a few kilometres north of here, and built the Cootharaba Sawmills, later adding a tramway to haul cedar logs from the hinterland. The mill closed in 1892. Boreen Point grew later; its estate blocks went to auction in 1933, and today it hosts sailing regattas.
